dossier.public_summary: The dip changes strongly between sectors and between individual transits, with only three deep events creating the signal. A faint secondary dip at phase 0.65 and a V-shaped grazing geometry point to a blended stellar eclipse rather than a 2-Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by 274% between sectors (verified: QLP p_constant 2.6279042432257057e-34, SPOC p_constant 2.580120684932191e-07, verdict changes_within_a_source). Alone not fatal but positive evidence for blend when combined with transit-to-transit scatter.

Single-transit depths inconsistent: top three carry share_of_top_3 0.854 and drive chi2 242.42221218988865 with dof 10, including outliers at 1744, 1704, 1753 ppm versus mean 514 ppm and nulls at -109, -110 ppm.

Second dip at phase 0.6539 depth 133.3 ppm depth_over_dip 0.2581 with snr above best_brightening 5.067 indicates stellar occultation; combined with odd_even diff_sigma 1.809 and Gaia excess_noise_sig 3.972 favours eclipsing binary over planet.

V-shaped transit (V test near 3) plus duration ratio 0.638 and fit_b 0.9983 grazing geometry together with density mismatch star_density_penalty 17.7 supports stellar eclipse, not a small planet - consistent with xgboost planet_rank 0.12.
